reasons.A: Short, clipped declaratives and a brisk plain-spoken tone are far from the passage's long, qualified, clause-laden sentences and reflective stance.
reasons.B: Long hedged sentences and rhetorical questions match the rhythm, but the hedges pile up (may be, arguably, in some sense, I suspect, it seems to me, perhaps), which reads as caricature, and the prescriptive close departs from the passage's observational stance.
reasons.C: Long sentences joined by semicolons and colon-led lists, varied by an occasional short one; a measured first-person hedge ('I have come to think', 'I suspect') and a reflective, diagnostic stance closest to the passage without overdoing its habits.
